name: The Fury Runs Deep
summary: Motley Garmason seeks vengeance against Kam Deepfury, now held in Stormwind's Stockade. Deepfury planned the assault on the Thandol Span, where Bronzebeard defenders died, including Longbraid the Grim's brother. Stormwind keeps Deepfury as a political prisoner, so Motley turns to an adventurer to carry out dwarven justice.

sections.title: A Grudge Across Continents
sections.body: Clashes between Bronzebeard defenders at Dun Modr and Dark Iron insurgents keep the northern Wetlands in turmoil. When the Thandol Span came under attack, sabotage took the lives of several dwarves, including Longbraid the Grim's brother. Roggo gathered intelligence showing that Kam Deepfury planned the strike. Rather than face execution on the front lines, Deepfury was taken to the Stormwind Stockade as a political prisoner, not executed for murder.

sections.title: Dwarven Retribution vs. Human Law
sections.body: Motley Garmason is stationed at Dun Modr and refuses to let Stormwind's political calculations shield a war criminal. To him, human law puts decorum before blood debts. Bound to remain beside Longbraid in the Wetlands, Motley sends trusted champions beneath the human capital, into the rioting Stockade, to take Deepfury's head and settle the clan's score.

faq.answer: Kam Deepfury is a Dark Iron dwarf who planned the attack on the Thandol Span. His plan led to the deaths of Ironforge dwarves guarding the crossing, and survivors in Dun Modr mark him as a target.

faq.q: Why is Kam Deepfury imprisoned in Stormwind instead of Ironforge?
faq.answer: Stormwind authorities captured Kam Deepfury and hold him in the Stockade for political reasons they have not disclosed. The dwarves of Dun Modr see this as bureaucracy that denies them immediate justice.

faq.q: Why doesn't Motley Garmason hunt Deepfury down himself?
faq.answer: Motley Garmason is stationed at Dun Modr beside Longbraid the Grim, where they face ongoing Dark Iron advances in the northern Wetlands. His honor and military duty keep him from leaving the defensive line for Stormwind.

faq.q: What happened at the Thandol Span?
faq.answer: The Dark Iron clan attacked the bridge at the Thandol Span, which connects the Wetlands to the Arathi Highlands. The assault killed several Bronzebeard defenders, including Longbraid's brother.

faq.q: Who uncovered Deepfury's role in the Thandol Span attack?
faq.answer: A dwarf named Roggo uncovered intelligence linking Kam Deepfury to the planning and execution of the Thandol Span attack. Roggo gave Motley the proof he needed to demand retribution.

faq.q: Is Stormwind's leadership aware of the assassination inside their prison?
faq.answer: Motley's order is an unsanctioned dwarven vendetta. He bypasses human law, believing King Magni's soldiers have the right to execute the saboteur while the Stockade is in the grip of riots.

angles.text: For Bronzebeard dwarves, killing Deepfury settles a blood debt and honors the clanmates who died defending the Thandol Span.
As a human, you face your kingdom's diplomatic choices when you set aside Stormwind's prison policies to meet your dwarven allies' code of justice.
As an Alliance member, you see the strain between Stormwind's legal pragmatism and Ironforge's demand for direct vengeance in wartime.
